It has four enolizable $\alpha$-carbons: C1, C3, C5, and C7. Intramolecular aldol condensation favors the formation of stable five- or six-membered rings.

Case 1: Enolate formation at C1 and attack on C6.
The C1 carbanion attacks the C6 carbonyl carbon, forming a 6-membered ring. After dehydration, a double bond forms between C1 and C6. The original C2 becomes the ring carbonyl (C1'). The C6 carbon (now C3' of the ring) retains the ethyl group ($\text{-CH}_2\text{CH}_3$). This yields 3-ethylcyclohex-2-en-1-one.

Case 2: Enolate formation at C7 and attack on C2.
The C7 carbanion attacks the C2 carbonyl carbon, forming another 6-membered ring. Dehydration creates a double bond between C7 and C2. The original C6 becomes the ring carbonyl (C1'). The C7 carbon (now C2' of the ring) has a methyl group (from C8), and the C2 carbon (now C3' of the ring) has a methyl group (from C1). This yields 2,3-dimethylcyclohex-2-en-1-one.

The reaction of an acyl chloride with hydrogen gas in the presence of palladium supported on barium sulfate (Pd-BaSO4) is known as the Rosenmund reduction.

In this reaction, the acyl chloride is reduced to the corresponding aldehyde. Barium sulfate acts as a catalytic poison, preventing further reduction of the aldehyde to an alcohol.

Therefore, butanoyl chloride is reduced to butanal.

Answer: Butanal

3-Pentanone ($CH_3-CH_2-CO-CH_2-CH_3$) is a symmetrical ketone with $\alpha$-hydrogens at C2 and C4. In the presence of dilute NaOH, it forms an enolate at C2.

This enolate acts as a nucleophile and attacks the electrophilic carbonyl carbon of benzaldehyde ($C_6H_5-CHO$).

Heating the reaction mixture causes the intermediate $\beta$-hydroxy ketone to undergo dehydration (loss of a water molecule), forming the $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated ketone 'P'. The structure of 'P' is 1-phenyl-2-methylpent-1-en-3-one ($C_6H_5-CH=C(CH_3)-CO-CH_2-CH_3$).

The second step is the reductive ozonolysis of compound 'P' using $O_3$ followed by $Zn/H_2O$.

Ozonolysis cleaves the carbon-carbon double bond ($C=C$). The carbon atom attached to the phenyl ring becomes an aldehyde group, yielding benzaldehyde ($C_6H_5-CHO$).

The other carbon atom of the double bond, which is already part of the ketone chain, is oxidized to a ketone group. This converts the remaining fragment into pentane-2,3-dione ($CH_3-CH_2-CO-CO-CH_3$).

Therefore, the final products are benzaldehyde and pentane-2,3-dione.

questions.solution:
Esterification of carboxylic acids with alcohols is a nucleophilic acyl substitution reaction. The rate of this reaction is highly sensitive to steric hindrance around the carbonyl carbon of the carboxylic acid.

As the size and number of alkyl groups attached to the $\alpha$-carbon increase, the steric crowding around the carbonyl carbon increases, making the nucleophilic attack by the alcohol more difficult. This leads to a decrease in the rate of esterification.

(II) Acetic acid: $CH_3COOH$ (primary $\alpha$-carbon)
(III) Isobutyric acid: $(CH_3)_2CHCOOH$ (secondary $\alpha$-carbon)
(IV) Pivalic acid: $(CH_3)_3CCOOH$ (tertiary $\alpha$-carbon, maximum steric hindrance)

Therefore, the correct decreasing order of reactivity towards esterification is (I) > (II) > (III) > (IV).

Answer: (I) > (II) > (III) > (IV)

questions.question: An organic compound X ($\text{C}_9\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$) gives a red-orange precipitate with $2,4$-DNP reagent and a yellow precipitate upon heating with iodine and aqueous $\text{NaOH}$. Drastic oxidation of X with alkaline $\text{KMnO}_4$ followed by acidification yields a dicarboxylic acid Y. Upon heating, compound Y readily loses a molecule of water to produce an anhydride Z. The compound X is:
questions.solution:
Compound X ($\text{C}_9\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$) forms a red-orange precipitate with $2,4$-DNP, indicating the presence of a carbonyl group.

It gives a yellow precipitate with $\text{I}_2/\text{NaOH}$ (iodoform test), confirming the presence of a methyl ketone ($-\text{COCH}_3$) group.

Drastic oxidation of X yields a dicarboxylic acid Y, meaning there are two oxidizable side chains on the benzene ring. Since X has $9$ carbon atoms and contains a $-\text{COCH}_3$ group ($2$ carbons), the remaining $7$ carbons must form a methylphenyl group. Thus, X is a methylacetophenone isomer.

Heating Y produces an anhydride Z, which is characteristic of ortho-dicarboxylic acids (like phthalic acid). This implies the two side chains in X must be ortho to each other.

Therefore, X is $1$-(2-methylphenyl)ethanone (o-methylacetophenone).

Answer: $1$-(2-Methylphenyl)ethanone

$\text{NaBH}_4$ is a mild reducing agent. It exhibits chemoselectivity by reducing the ketone group in the 2-oxopropyl side chain to a secondary alcohol, but it does not reduce the ester group.

Thus, the major product is methyl 2-(prop-1-en-1-yl)benzoate.

This substitutes one $\alpha$-hydrogen with a chlorine atom, yielding 2-chloroethanoic acid ($\text{Cl}-\text{CH}_2-\text{COOH}$) as compound (B).

Answer: 2-Chloroethanoic acid

If X were incorrectly identified as propanal, the final product would be but-2-enoic acid, but propanal does not give a positive iodoform test.

Answer: 2-Methylprop-2-enoic acid

questions.question: An organic compound A ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}$) gives a yellow precipitate with 2,4-DNP reagent but does not reduce Tollens' reagent. questions.solution:
A positive 2,4-DNP test indicates that compound A is a carbonyl compound (aldehyde or ketone).

A negative Tollens' test confirms that compound A is a ketone, as aldehydes are easily oxidized by Tollens' reagent.

The molecular formula $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}$ corresponds to a saturated acyclic ketone.

Drastic oxidation of ketones involves C-C bond cleavage. The fact that symmetrical cleavage yields two molecules of a single carboxylic acid implies the ketone itself must be symmetrical.

The only symmetrical acyclic ketone with the formula $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}$ is hexan-3-one ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3$).

Symmetrical cleavage of hexan-3-one (between C3 and C4) yields two molecules of propanoic acid ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$), which is compound B.

Hexan-2-one is unsymmetrical and its cleavage yields a mixture of different acids without a symmetrical cleavage option. Hexanal is an aldehyde and would give a positive Tollens' test. Cyclohexanol is an alcohol and would not give a positive 2,4-DNP test.

Answer: A = Hexan-3-one ; B = Propanoic acid
